The reference **butterfly correlation** (via the GitHub-only `ggcor` package) arranges two groups gene-to-pathway correlations as a mirrored heatmap with **links from one gene to all pathways** \[1\]. This tutorial **re-implements the layout in plain ggplot2** (ggcor is GitHub-only) from a simulated pathway-score matrix:

## Example

![](../images/Correlation/LinkCorPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="Butterfly Correlation Heatmap DEMO" fig-align="center" width="60%"}

## Setup

-   System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)

-   Programming language: R

-   Dependent packages: `ggplot2`; `dplyr`

```{r packages setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, output=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(dplyr)
})
```

```{r}
sessioninfo::session_info("attached")
```

## Data Preparation

One gene correlated against 12 pathways in two simulated cohorts - the butterfly puts cohort A below and cohort B above, with links radiating from the query gene:

```{r load data}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(ggplot2); library(dplyr)})
set.seed(22801)
pathways <- paste0("Path", sprintf("%02d", 1:12))
n_sam <- 80
gene_a <- rnorm(n_sam)
pathA <- do.call(cbind, lapply(pathways, function(p)
  gene_a * runif(1, -0.8, 0.8) + rnorm(n_sam, 0, 0.6)))
colnames(pathA) <- pathways
gene_b <- rnorm(n_sam)
pathB <- do.call(cbind, lapply(pathways, function(p)
  gene_b * runif(1, -0.5, 0.5) + rnorm(n_sam, 0, 0.8)))
colnames(pathB) <- pathways
corr_test <- function(expr_vec, score_mat) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(pathways, function(p) {
    ct <- cor.test(expr_vec, score_mat[, p])
    data.frame(pathway = p, r = as.numeric(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value)
  }))
}
cA <- corr_test(gene_a, pathA); cA$cohort <- "Cohort A"
cB <- corr_test(gene_b, pathB); cB$cohort <- "Cohort B"
all_c <- rbind(cA, cB)
all_c$sig <- cut(all_c$p, c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
                 labels = c("p<0.001", "p<0.01", "p<0.05", "ns"))
all_c$absw <- cut(abs(all_c$r), c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
                  labels = c("0.25", "0.50", "0.75", "1.00"))
```

## Visualization

### 1. Butterfly Correlation Links

The ggplot2 re-implementation: tiles for the correlation matrix with links radiating from the query gene to each significant pathway:

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1LinkCor
#| fig-cap: "Butterfly correlation heatmap of a query gene against 12 simulated pathways in two cohorts: line colour = significance class, linewidth = |r| bin, radiating from the query gene."
#| out.width: "85%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5

ggplot(all_c, aes(pathway, cohort)) +
  geom_tile(fill = "grey95", colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = pathway, xend = pathway,
                   y = ifelse(cohort == "Cohort A", 1.15, 1.85),
                   yend = ifelse(cohort == "Cohort A", 2.0, 1.0),
                   colour = sig, linewidth = absw, linetype = sig),
               data = all_c[all_c$p < 0.05, ], alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("p<0.001" = "#B2182B", "p<0.01" = "#EF8A62",
                                 "p<0.05" = "#67A9CF"), name = "Significance") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("p<0.001" = "solid", "p<0.01" = "solid",
                                   "p<0.05" = "22"), guide = "none") +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c("0.25" = 0.3, "0.50" = 0.6, "0.75" = 0.9, "1.00" = 1.2), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Gene-to-pathway correlation butterfly (simulated)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey40"))
```

::: callout-tip
**Practice tips**

-   The `ggcor` package (GitHub-only) cannot enter the lockfile - the butterfly layout is reproducible in plain ggplot2.
-   Two correlation matrices sharing the same pathway set can be arranged as a **butterfly** (one cohort per side) for cross-cohort comparison.
-   Bin |r| and P into **ordered categories** rather than mapping continuous values - the categorical encoding keeps gradients readable.
:::
